answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 6 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The tundra multiplier is published, charged in ivory, and spiral lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, as the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 2003 identities would post 714 proofs and burn roughly 77 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
